meta.title: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge Guide for Pokemon Red++
meta.compatibility: The user-supplied guide targets Red++ 4.5.3 while runtime RAM mapping targets 3.0.2. Route, encounter and evolution facts are advisory; observed v3.0.2 RAM is authoritative.
meta.rewardPolicy: Guide content supplies context and curriculum only. It never defines numeric reinforcement rewards.

principles: Red++ adds later-generation Pokemon, Dark/Steel/Fairy types, physical-special split and altered evolution methods.
Headbutt trees, breeding without egg hatching and location-based evolutions are useful optional collection mechanics.
Keep attacking moves and PP coverage while grinding; do not replace all weak attacks with status moves.
The Oak challenge's catch-everything gates are optional because the active objective is becoming Champion quickly.

championRoute.objective: Choose a starter and finish Oak's opening sequence
Defeat Brock for the Boulder Badge
Defeat Misty for the Cascade Badge and Cut access
Get the Secret Key and defeat Blaine
Defeat Giovanni for the Earth Badge
Defeat the Elite Four and Champion

locations.name: Pallet Town
locations.summary: Choose Bulbasaur, Charmander or Squirtle. Bulbasaur reaches its final form four levels earlier, but all starters can work.

objectives.name: Choose a starter Pokemon
objectives.description: Complete Oak's opening sequence and obtain the first party member.

locations.name: Route 1
locations.summary: Early catches; Zigzagoon can learn Pay Day and Headbutt.

locations.name: Viridian City
locations.summary: Opening hub between Pallet Town, Route 22 and Viridian Forest.
objectives: Complete Oak's parcel and Pokedex sequence

locations.name: Route 22
locations.summary: Optional early rival battle and several useful catches.

locations.name: Viridian Forest
locations.summary: Catch the early bug lines and Pikachu; a spare Pikachu enables the Pewter museum trade.
objectives: Traverse Viridian Forest to Pewter City

locations.name: Pewter City
locations.summary: Brock is the first mandatory progression wall. Optional: trade a spare Pikachu for Togepi; Headbutt trees add Red++ encounters.

objectives.name: Defeat Brock for the Boulder Badge
objectives.description: Unlock the eastern route from Pewter City.

locations.name: Route 3
locations.summary: Progress east after Brock; Magikarp can be trained on preserved trainers.

locations.name: Route 4
locations.summary: A Magikarp is available from the Pokemon Center salesman before Mt. Moon.

locations.name: Mt. Moon
locations.summary: Red++ allows returning after the ledges. Mt. Moon Square sells Moon Stones; collect both fossils on the way out.

locations.name: Cerulean City
locations.summary: Use this hub for Nugget Bridge, Bill, the bike and the second mandatory badge.

objectives.name: Defeat Misty for the Cascade Badge
objectives.description: Enables Cut progression in this Red++ route.

locations.name: Route 24
locations.summary: Catch Abra, Oddish and Bellsprout; continue to Bill for the S.S. Ticket.
objectives: Visit Bill and obtain the S.S. Ticket

locations.name: Route 5
locations.summary: The daycare supplies a Ditto and breeding completes immediately after enough steps rather than egg hatching.

locations.name: Vermilion City
locations.summary: Collect the Old Rod and Bike Voucher; Red++ trades can supply Squirtle.
objectives: Prepare and board the S.S. Anne

locations.name: Route 11
locations.summary: Headbutt trees add Exeggcute and Heracross.

locations.name: Diglett Cave
locations.summary: Connects Vermilion to Route 2 and the Abra-for-Sneasel trade.

objectives.name: Use Diglett Cave for Route 2 access

locations.name: Route 2
locations.summary: Trade a spare Abra for Sneasel; Moon Stone evolves it to Weavile.

locations.name: S.S. Anne
locations.summary: Clear the ship and obtain HM01 Cut before it departs permanently.

locations.name: Route 9
locations.summary: Cut opens the eastern route toward Rock Tunnel.

locations.name: Route 10
locations.summary: Red++ adds Skarmory, Bellossom and other useful encounters before Rock Tunnel.

locations.name: Rock Tunnel
locations.summary: Flash helps but is not required; Ditto and Torkoal are Red++ additions to the route knowledge.

locations.name: Route 8
locations.summary: Western route from Lavender toward Celadon.

locations.name: Celadon City
locations.summary: Get Eevee, stones and Porygon; clear Rocket Hideout for the Silph Scope. Location-based and stone evolutions differ from vanilla Red.
objectives: Clear Rocket Hideout and obtain the Silph Scope
Defeat Erika for the Rainbow Badge and Strength access

locations.name: Route 16
locations.summary: Cut accesses grass and Fly; Cycling Road leads toward Fuchsia.

locations.name: Lavender Town
locations.summary: Use the Silph Scope in Pokemon Tower, rescue Mr. Fuji and obtain the Poke Flute.

locations.name: Route 12
locations.summary: Wake Snorlax and obtain the Super Rod while heading south.

locations.name: Fuchsia City
locations.summary: Collect the rods and Exp. Share; Koga is prioritized because his badge unlocks Surf.
objectives: Defeat Koga for the Soul Badge and Surf access

locations.name: Safari Zone
locations.summary: HM03 Surf and Gold Teeth are progression-critical; Gold Teeth trade for Strength.
objectives: Find Gold Teeth and obtain Strength

locations.name: Saffron City
locations.summary: Clear Silph Co., receive Lapras and later defeat Sabrina. The Fighting Dojo supports the Tyrogue line.
objectives: Defeat Sabrina for the Marsh Badge

locations.name: Power Plant
locations.summary: Surf access opens Zapdos and Red++ location evolutions for Magneton, Porygon2 and Electabuzz.

objectives.name: Optional Power Plant catches and evolutions

locations.name: Cinnabar Island
locations.summary: Revive fossils, explore Pokemon Mansion for the Secret Key and Old Sea Map, then defeat Blaine.
objectives: Find the Secret Key in Pokemon Mansion
Defeat Blaine for the Volcano Badge

locations.name: Seafoam Islands
locations.summary: B4F enables Glaceon. Strength solves the boulder-current puzzle and opens Articuno.

locations.name: Faraway Island
locations.summary: The Old Sea Map unlocks the ferry to the static level-30 Mew encounter.

sections.title: Parts 5-6 - Remaining Badges and Elite Four Access

locations.name: Vermilion City
locations.summary: Lt. Surge can be delayed in the Oak route because Fly does not unlock new species, but his badge is required for the League.
objectives: Defeat Lt. Surge for the Thunder Badge

locations.name: Viridian City
locations.summary: Return after the other badges and defeat Giovanni.
objectives: Defeat Giovanni for the Earth Badge

locations.name: Victory Road
locations.summary: Cross the final cave and optionally catch Moltres. Three legendary birds unlock the Mystic Ticket at Cinnabar Lab.
objectives: Cross Victory Road and reach Indigo Plateau

locations.name: Navel Rock
locations.summary: The Mystic Ticket unlocks optional level-40 Lugia and Ho-Oh encounters.

locations.name: Indigo Plateau
locations.summary: Final sequence: defeat Lorelei, Bruno, Agatha, Lance and the Champion.

locations.name: Cerulean Cave
locations.summary: Post-Champion cave containing the final level-70 Mewtwo encounter.
